title: 5th Sitting of second session of 2025
summary: The sitting ran from 9:02 to 11:15. Members questioned the Minister of Construction, Housing and Infrastructure about stalled water, sewerage, road, harbour and housing projects across many islands. The Majlis agreed to debate and then refer a privilege complaint (about access to a special-needs centre in K. Guraidhoo) to committee, accepted a resolution on the decentralisation law for committee study (52-11), and approved two non-resident ambassador nominations (Ireland, Ukraine). Some text is garbled, so counts and gists are best-effort.

items.title: Attendance of members
items.outcome: 35 present, 8 on leave, 5 on official travel at the start

items.title: Questions to the Minister of Construction, Housing and Infrastructure (Dr. Abdulla Muaththalib)
items.outcome: Debated; 24 member questions and follow-ups, minister answered 23 and declined one as unrelated

items.title: Privilege matter raised by North Galolhu MP Mohamed Ibrahim (rule 208) over access to the K. Guraidhoo special-needs centre
items.outcome: Debate accepted 55-0; later referred to the Privileges and Conduct Committee 63-0

items.title: Resolution by Kanditheemu MP Ameen Faisal on overtime pay and fair working conditions for education and health workers
Resolution by Baarashu MP Ibrahim Shuja seeking members' views on problems in the Decentralisation Act (Law 2010/7), third day of debate
items.outcome: Debate closed; accepted 52-11 and sent to the Decentralisation Committee

items.title: Foreign Relations Committee report on non-resident ambassador nominations for Ireland and Ukraine
Votes on pending matters
items.outcome: Four votes taken: privilege referral, decentralisation resolution, Ireland ambassador, Ukraine ambassador

speakers.name: Dr. Abdulla Muaththalib
positions: As Construction, Housing and Infrastructure minister: Kudarikilu, Kihaadhoo and Dhonfanu sewerage restarted under MWSC; completion targeted September 2026; many projects stuck awaiting URA approvals.
Said housing loans are government-subsidised through financial institutions; agreements being signed, lending to start after eligibility checks, applications going to banks around early July.
Said the Addu Link Road site is being finalised for mobilisation, with works to start once fixed. Declined some questions as unrelated to the day's topic.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked when stalled water and sewerage work in Kudarikilu, Kihaadhoo and Dhonfanu would start and finish; said Kendhoo's system is finished but not serving residents.
Backed sending the privilege motion to committee, citing MPs' duty to oversee state institutions.
In the decentralisation debate, said council reform should not erode public trust in councils and questioned cutting councils while political posts grow.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked when Ulaidhoo road work, Kurinbee housing signing and Vaikaradhoo's finished sewerage service would begin.
On the ambassador report, backed the committee's diligence but argued the Majlis agenda is crowded with President's Office submissions and ministers need to deliver more.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked when FDC flats will be handed over per the President's pledge and whether applicants left out have been told.
Raised a privilege complaint: the Health Minister did not answer his 19 April letter seeking access to the K. Guraidhoo special-needs centre.
Argued the law on Majlis privileges requires ministries to arrange such visits and urged action on unanswered MP letters.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Asked when harbour and road works at Kelaa, where the beach is eroding, and Fillaadhoo road and reclamation would be finished.
In the decentralisation debate, said 15 years of amendments have not produced good results and welcomed gathering MPs' views.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Asked when ministry works on islands in his constituency would start and whether delays stem from the previous government.
Moved referral of the privilege matter to committee; said the Majlis should accept useful motions from any party and blamed the centre's condition on the previous government.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Argued MPs should debate in citizens' interest and that jobs near resorts and in waste management should go to Maldivians rather than expatriates.
Said 15 years of decentralisation amendments have not resolved the problems and criticised the opposition's arguments as politically driven.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Said Manadhoo's sewerage, installed in 2014, lacks spares and sewage is flowing into the island; asked for a permanent fix and timeline.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked whether the minister knows Hithadhoo's sewerage is poorly maintained and overflowing, and when residents will get a solution.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked when planned housing units in Fuvahmulah would start and why the work is stalled.

speakers.name: Ashraf Rasheed
positions: Asked about Rathafandhoo harbour and shore protection, flooding concerns, and when Faresmaathodaa's land reclamation would begin.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Asked when unfinished water and sewerage work in Feheendhoo and Fulhadhoo would restart and when residents would get service.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Asked when the northern reclaimed land in Thinadhoo, reclaimed around 2016-17, would get water and sewerage.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Asked about Kunahandhoo water and sewerage work handed to MWSC but not started, and where the ministry's responsibility ends after handover.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Said his question was unrelated to the day's topic and thanked the minister for the ministry's work.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked when practical work on the Addu Link Road would begin, citing residents' difficulties and damage to vehicles.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Asked when completed water and sewerage in Feydhoo, Goidhoo and Bilehfahi would serve residents and about hookups for new houses in Kanditheemu.

speakers.name: Ahmed Riyaz
positions: Asked about response to the Vaemandhoo-Kinbidhoo causeway, a Bandaara plot letter from the council, and Thimarafushi harbour upgrade work.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naufal
positions: Said about 100 completed houses in Kolhufushi remain unhanded to residents without utilities, despite the President's pledge, and asked for a solution.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Asked when practical work on the Addu bridge would begin and whether vehicles for Addu road works have reached the company.

speakers.name: Adam Shafeeq
positions: Asked when Makunudhoo and Neykurendhoo water and sewerage work would finish and when airport works would start, citing residents' isolation.

speakers.name: Mohamed Siruhaan
positions: Asked for the date the completed Dharavandhoo sewerage will be formally handed over.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Citing statistics, said about MVR 1.5bn (11%) of this year's MVR 12.3bn PSIP budget had been spent; asked whether works or releases of funds are lagging.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Asked for an update on the announced housing loans and when funds will be released.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Asked why Diddoo bridge work has been stalled for a long time and when it will restart.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: Questioned whether a Majlis view would settle a 15-year dispute and urged cross-party consultation.
Said council grants and local tourism promotion trips have mixed value; supported overhauling the system but not cutting councils alone.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Presented the Foreign Relations Committee report: both nominees already serve as ambassadors, so no further interviews or documents were sought.
Said the committee approved both nominations unanimously among members voting, at its meeting on 16 June 2025.

decisions: North Galolhu MP's privilege complaint accepted for debate (55-0) and referred to the Privileges and Conduct Committee (63-0).
Decentralisation Act resolution accepted 52-11 and sent to the Decentralisation Committee for study.
Nomination of H. Orchid, Alfadila Irtisham Adam as non-resident ambassador to Ireland approved 66-0.
Nomination of M. Geelaavila, Alfadila Qeela Ali as non-resident ambassador to Ukraine approved 66-0.
Resolution on overtime pay and working conditions for education and health workers had its first reading.
Chair announced the next sitting for Monday 23 June 2025 at 9:00.

votes.what: Debate the privilege complaint raised by North Galolhu MP Mohamed Ibrahim
Refer the privilege complaint to the relevant committee (Privileges and Conduct)
Accept the Decentralisation Act resolution and send to the Decentralisation Committee
Appoint non-resident ambassador to Ireland (Irtisham Adam)
Appoint non-resident ambassador to Ukraine (Qeela Ali)
